sections.h2: What is the Sugar Land city property tax rate?
sections.html:
The City of Sugar Land says its adopted rate for Tax Year 2026 is $0.371116 per $100 of taxable value, adopted after a public hearing on September 8, 2026. That figure covers only the city share of a Sugar Land bill; the school district, Fort Bend County and any MUD or LID levy sit on top of it.

The city splits its rate into two parts: $0.220157 for maintenance and operations and $0.150959 for debt service. Debt service is the portion that repays borrowed money for city projects.

On its own page the city also notes that it makes up about 21 percent of the residential bill in Fort Bend ISD and 19 percent in Lamar CISD, before any MUD or LID taxes. Which district serves your house is printed on your tax bill.

sections.h2: How have Sugar Land's rates changed over three years?
sections.html:
The rate edged up in both Tax Year 2025 and Tax Year 2026. The city publishes a three-year comparison, reproduced below as printed on its site.

City of Sugar Land tax rate per $100, as printed on sugarlandtx.gov

Maintenance and operations$0.220157$0.207172$0.207172
Debt service$0.150959$0.151655$0.146038
Total$0.371116$0.358827$0.353210

The city also lists a no-new-revenue rate of $0.355381 and a voter-approval rate of $0.381586 for 2026. The voter-approval rate is the ceiling the city cannot pass without a vote. For the median homestead the city prints an estimated annual city bill of $1,371 for 2026, against $1,312 the prior year.

sections.h2: How does Sugar Land set its rate each year?
sections.html:
Council adopts the rate in September, after budget approval and a public hearing. The city has 60 days after it receives the certified tax roll, or until September 30, whichever is later, to adopt it. For 2025 the council adopted $0.358827 on September 16, 2025, by Ordinance No. 2387, and for 2026 the hearing was held September 8, 2026.

Two reference rates frame the vote. The no-new-revenue rate raises the same money as the year before from existing property, and the voter-approval rate is the most the city can set without an election. The city describes the voter-approval rate as the revenue needed for debt service plus a 3.5 percent increase in maintenance and operations revenue.

The city also publishes a taxpayer impact statement, stating a $4.90 monthly impact for the median homestead in 2026, and budgeted property tax revenue of $81,205,666 for FY2027. Appraised values are certified by July 25, so the rate cannot be final until that roll is in.

sections.h2: Which exemptions does Sugar Land offer?
sections.html:
The city lists a homestead exemption of 15 percent of assessed value, plus $70,000 for owners who are over 65 and $70,000 for disabled persons. Someone who is both over 65 and disabled gets just one. For disabled veterans, the city tells owners to contact the Fort Bend Central Appraisal District.

These are the city's exemptions. School districts have their own, and the Texas Comptroller prints the state-required school homestead exemption as $140,000, with another $60,000 for seniors and disabled owners. Older and disabled owners also get a school tax ceiling that generally holds the school bill at the level of the year they first qualified.

  • Ownership and main-residence use are required, with no second homestead claimed anywhere.
  • A purchaser closing after New Year's Day can claim for the remainder of that tax year if the seller never did.
  • Applications go to the appraisal district, not to the city.

sections.h2: Who sets the value and who collects the tax in Sugar Land?
sections.html:
Values come from the Fort Bend Central Appraisal District, while billing and collecting fall to the Fort Bend County Tax Assessor-Collector. The city says it contracts with the county assessor-collector for billing and collection, and it sends exemption and valuation questions to the appraisal district.

The appraisal district's office is at 2801 B F Terry Blvd, Rosenberg, TX 77471, and its phone is 281-344-8623, as printed on the Fort Bend County exemption page. That page also says exemption applications need a copy of the applicant's Texas driver's license or DPS ID, and the address on it must match the property address.

Texas appraises property as of January 1. Under the state calendar, notices for single-family homesteads go out around April 1, protests are generally due mid-May, and the appraisal records are approved in July. A value you dispute has to be challenged inside that window.

sections.h2: What is the payment deadline in Sugar Land?
sections.html:
Pay by January 31. A Sugar Land bill that is still open on February 1 counts as delinquent, per the Comptroller's statewide schedule.

Two details help. If the bill was mailed after January 10, the cutoff slides to the first day of a later month that leaves at least 21 days. Seniors and disabled owners may split the bill into four installments.

  • On February 1 a six percent penalty and one percent interest are added.
  • The penalty keeps climbing monthly until it hits 12 percent on July 1.
  • Interest has no cap, and a collection lawyer's fee of up to 20 percent can follow.

sections.h2: Does the tax bill follow a Sugar Land house to a new owner?
sections.html:
Yes, in the sense that the lien stays on the land. It attaches on January 1, and the person who owned the house that day can still be sued for the year's tax after selling.

For that reason the closing agent asks for a tax certificate and pays what is owed out of seller funds. An unpaid account moves through notices, an optional installment plan and finally a suit, with costs added. A taxing unit can ultimately foreclose and auction the house.

If back taxes are the reason you want to sell, call the Fort Bend County Tax Assessor-Collector for a payoff number before pricing. With that figure you can weigh an agent listing, a private deal and a cash offer evenly. Penalty and interest can sometimes be waived when the tax is paid soon after you learn of the delinquency, so raise that with the tax office too.

faqs.q: What is the 2026 city tax rate in Sugar Land?
faqs.a: $0.371116 per $100 of taxable value, per the City of Sugar Land's adopted-rate page. School, county and any MUD or LID rates come on top.

faqs.q: Does Sugar Land give a homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Yes: 15 percent of assessed value, plus $70,000 for over-65 owners or $70,000 for disabled persons, one of the two at most. File with the Fort Bend Central Appraisal District.

faqs.q: Who gets my Sugar Land tax payment?
faqs.a: The Fort Bend County Tax Assessor-Collector, which collects for the city by contract. Value and exemption questions go to the appraisal district.

faqs.q: When does a Sugar Land bill go delinquent?
faqs.a: After January 31. February 1 brings a six percent penalty and one percent interest.

faqs.q: Can I sell if I owe taxes on my Sugar Land house?
faqs.a: Yes. The closing agent pays the balance with your proceeds, so get a payoff figure from the county tax office first.
